correctness.rationale: Exact conditional Gaussian and beta age laws give the finite-\(N\) binomial mixture and inverted CDF. Endpoint Taylor and Gaussian-tail expansions give both edge shapes. Binomial CLT with Hoeffding domination proves \(N^{-\theta/2}\) finite-population rounding for every positive \(\theta\); the gamma integral verifies its explicit coefficient. A two-sided elementary Tauberian sandwich proves \(\Pr(K_N=N)\sim ra^2/(4D\log N)\). The standalone deterministic verification script passed 68 assertions over distinct parameter sets. All limits assume fixed positive parameters; numerical checks do not establish infinite statements.

For free Brownian particles, 2025 full counting work has an equilibrium-window probability tending to zero as reset age increases, whereas harmonic confinement leaves \(p_*=\operatorname{erf}(a\sqrt{\mu/(2D)})>0\).

The new finite-\(N\) lower-edge event scales \(N^{-r/(4\mu)}\) with an explicit Gaussian convolution and gamma coefficient. This requires the distinct \(p_*>0\), \(q(y)-p_*\sim By\) boundary structure and does not follow as a stated special case from the accessible unconfined-gas results.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is the paired finite-population counting-edge theorem for a common-reset, harmonic OU gas: a positive equilibrium floor with tunable \(N^{-r/(4\mu)}\) Gaussian-rounded lower-edge probability and a contrasting inverse-logarithmic all-inside event. The conditional-IID mixture and the unconfined free-Brownian counting framework are prior art, explicitly credited. The identifiable 2026 confined-gas source emphasizes edge order statistics and does not claim these specific bulk counting-edge results in the accessible original abstract; a detailed scientific review reports full counting as a gap. Source-full-text access and broad-mixture subsumption remain stated risks.

value.rationale: The finite-population occupancy of a central optical observation window is a natural bulk statistic complementary to known extreme/gap observables. The theorem gives a complete compact-support bulk law, a continuously tunable lower-edge density phase transition at \(r=2\mu\) and an explicit \(N^{-r/(4\mu)}\) Gaussian-rounded rare-event profile, compared against a universal \(1/\log N\) all-inside event. The precise two-edge finite-size distinction is useful for distinguishing long-age equilibration from short-age common-reset intermittency; it is not a mere normalization check or an arbitrary parameter slice.
